items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the agriculture and markets law, in relation to protection for timber operations from unreasonably restrictive ordinances and correction of errors in agricultural district review filings
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S7100

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the agriculture and markets law, in relation to
protection for timber operations from unreasonably restrictive
ordinances and correction of errors in agricultural district review
filings


 PURPOSE OF THE BILL :

The bill would clarify protection for timber operations from
unreasonably restrictive ordinances, clarify which woodland acreage is
eligible to receive such protection, and clarify how counties may
request the Commissioner's approval to correct errors made in their
filings with the Department of Agriculture and Markets (Department).

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section 1 of the bill would amend Agriculture and Markets Law (AML) §
301 (11) to define a "farm operation" to include a "timber operation"
as defined in an amended AML § 301(14). Section 1 of the bill would
also amend AML § 301(11) by removing the production, management and
harvesting of farm woodland from the definition.

Section 2 of the bill would amend AML § 301(14) to define the term
"timber operation" to mean the on-farm production, management,
harvesting, processing and marketing of timber grown on the farm
operation.

Section 3 of the bill would amend AML § 303-a (5) to clarify the
process for correcting errors in agricultural district review filings
with the Department.

Section 4 of the bill would amend AML § 308(1)(b) to make conforming
amendments due to the proposed amendment of the definition for "farm
operation" in AML § 308(11).

Section 5 of the bill would provide for an immediate effective date.

 EXISTING LAW :

AML § 301(11) defines a "farm operation" to include "timber
processing" and the production, management and harvesting of "farm
woodland."

AML § 301(14) defines "timber processing" as the on-farm processing of
timber grown on a farm operation into woodland products, including but
not limited to logs, lumber, posts and firewood, through the use of a
readily moveable, nonpermanent saw mill.

AML § 303-a (5) provides for the review, certification and filing of
agricultural district review plans.

AML § 308(1)(b) sets forth examples of agricultural practices listed
in the Right to Farm Law, including the production, management and
harvesting of farm woodland.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

This is a new proposal.

 STATEMENT IN SUPPORT :


The United States Department of Agriculture's 2007 Census of
Agriculture reports that over one fifth of land in New York farms
consists of woodland. Farm woodland, and the production for sale of
woodland products, has long been recognized as eligible for an
agricultural value assessment subject to acreage and gross sales
limitations. An amendment to the AML enacted in 2005, along with two
additional amendments enacted in 2008, added on-farm timber processing
activities to Article 25-AA of the Agriculture and Markets Law
relating to agricultural districts.

This bill is necessary to consolidate and clarify confusing aspects of
these amendments as they relate to the protections and benefits
afforded farm timber operations. Specifically, the definition of "farm
operation" incorporates the terms "timber processing" and "farm
woodland" that are each separately defined. The inclusion of both
these terms is incongruous because the latter term exists for
agricultural assessment purposes to identify a type of land. In
contrast, it is used in the term "farm operation" to identify a type
of crop. Thus, the bill would harmonize the terms by removing the term
"farm woodland" and associated language from the definition of "farm
operation."

Conversely, the definition of the term "timber processing" does not
accurately describe all the relevant timber-related activities that
should be covered by the statute, including marketing. Therefore, the
bill would add marketing to that term, change the term to "timber
operation," and add conforming language previously associated with
"farm woodland" within the definition of "farm operation." As a
result, the bill would provide better notice to landowners and
municipalities of their rights and responsibilities, and would assist
the Department in the efficient administration of the agricultural
districts law. However, by retaining the sales thresholds currently in
the definition of the term "timber processing," the bill would limit
such protections to timber operations that have ~ substantial
connection to a farm.

 BUDGET IMPLICATIONS :

None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
The bill would take effect immediately.

summary: Provides protection for timber operations from unreasonably restrictive ordinances, pertains to correction of errors in agricultural district review filings.
